summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 25%), ICD, chronic kidney disease, and recent heart failure exacerbation was admitted for altered mental status, nausea, and vomiting following increased Percocet use for a right humeral fracture. Evaluation revealed no acute intracranial or abdominal pathology on imaging, and labs showed stable renal function with mild hyperkalemia. Symptoms were attributed to opiate toxicity, exacerbated by reduced kidney clearance. Percocet was discontinued, mental status improved, and pain was transitioned to Vicodin with close monitoring. Lisinopril was restarted, spironolactone held due to hyperkalemia, and heart failure management continued with torsemide. The patient was discharged home with improved cognition, stable labs, and follow-up plans for labs, primary care, and cardiology.
